_comment: Ingredients matched here scale fine arithmetically, but a fractional result implies an awkward, perishable, or hard-to-store leftover (half a can, part of a bottle, etc). 'keyword' is matched as a case-insensitive substring against each parsed ingredient name. These produce a note, not a blocker, unlike non_scalable.json.

ingredients.note: Canned coconut milk doesn't keep well once opened. A fractional amount means leftover you'll need to use within a few days or freeze.
This usually comes in one can size. A fractional amount leaves an open can with a short fridge life.
Buttermilk is usually sold in larger containers than most recipes use. A fractional amount means more leftover to use up before it spoils.
Heavy cream has a limited fridge life once opened. A small fractional amount may be more than you'll use before it turns.
Cream cheese is usually sold in fixed block sizes. A fractional amount leaves a partial block to store and use up.
